one_line_reason: Multiple controlled crossover/RCTs show oral Mucuna pruriens seed powder (a natural L-DOPA source) matches or outperforms standard levodopa in Parkinson's disease, plus one separate trial shows benefit for male infertility, but all PD evidence is drug-like dosing in a clinical population.

selected.population: adults with advanced Parkinson's disease and motor fluctuations (n=18, double-blind, randomized, controlled, crossover)
selected.intervention: Mucuna pruriens seed powder (roasted, unprocessed), oral, single doses, vs. standard levodopa+dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor and placebo
selected.dose_as_stated: high-dose MP 17.5 mg/kg or low-dose MP 12.5 mg/kg (levodopa content basis)
selected.primary_outcome: motor response at 90/180 minutes and duration of ON state
selected.why_selected: highest-quality controlled design in the shortlist (double-blind, placebo arm included) with a clearly stated body-weight-based dose and a positive, non-inferior-to-superior result versus standard levodopa.

selected.population: untreated Parkinson's disease patients in sub-Saharan Africa (n=32, 12-month, multicenter, randomized, open-label)
selected.intervention: Mucuna pruriens powder (from roasted seeds), oral, dose adjusted for body weight and disease stage, vs. standard levodopa + dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor
selected.dose_as_stated: not stated (individually titrated by body weight/disease stage)
selected.primary_outcome: quality of life (PDQ-39) and motor/non-motor disability (MDS-UPDRS)
selected.why_selected: longest-duration (12-month) and most real-world trial in the shortlist, showing MP non-inferior to standard levodopa on all endpoints.

selected.intervention: Mucuna pruriens seed powder treatment, oral (prospective clinical study)
selected.primary_outcome: sperm concentration, motility, and seminal plasma biochemical/antioxidant markers
selected.why_selected: the only shortlisted trial addressing a non-Parkinson's outcome (male fertility), which is closer to why general catalog Mucuna products are typically marketed (testosterone/fertility support).

selected.population: 8 Parkinson's disease patients with short-duration L-dopa response and dyskinesias (double-blind, randomized, crossover)
selected.intervention: Mucuna pruriens seed powder preparation, oral, single doses, vs. standard levodopa/carbidopa
selected.dose_as_stated: 15 g or 30 g of mucuna preparation
selected.primary_outcome: L-dopa pharmacokinetics, UPDRS score, tapping speed, dyskinesia severity
selected.why_selected: small but well-controlled crossover trial with a clear gram-based dose (closer to a label-mappable supplement amount than mg/kg dosing) showing faster onset and longer ON time than standard levodopa.

blockers: All Parkinson's disease trials dose Mucuna like a drug (mg/kg or gram amounts titrated to replace scheduled levodopa) in a diagnosed clinical population, not the general-use context (energy, libido, testosterone) that catalog generic/sports Mucuna products are typically marketed for.

Because Mucuna's active constituent is natural L-DOPA, using it as a self-directed levodopa substitute raises safety concerns not relevant to typical supplement doses — one crossover trial (29352722, not selected) found 50% of patients discontinued due to GI side effects or worsening motor symptoms.
The one non-PD outcome (male fertility, 18001713) is an older study without a clearly described placebo-controlled design in the abstract, and gives no dose.

handoff_pmids.note: Small (n=7) crossover pharmacokinetic study of Japanese-grown Mucuna pruriens (11 g single dose) in Parkinson's patients; shows prolonged L-dopa ON time and a COMT-inhibitory-like metabolite pattern versus standard levodopa/carbidopa, but is framed around pharmacokinetics rather than a clinical efficacy endpoint.

excluded_pmids.reason: Narrative review of plant-derived neuroprotective compounds in Parkinson's disease that mentions L-DOPA derived from Mucuna pruriens only as one example among many phytochemicals; not primary trial data and redundant with the actual Mucuna RCTs already selected.
Food-science/biochemistry review of enzymatic production of ACE-inhibitory peptides from soybean and velvet bean protein hydrolysates; not a human supplementation efficacy study.

16-week crossover pilot RCT of Mucuna pruriens vs. standard levodopa/carbidopa in advanced Parkinson's disease; efficacy was similar in patients who tolerated it, but half discontinued due to GI side effects or worsening motor performance, making tolerability the dominant finding rather than clean efficacy.
Open-label (uncontrolled, unblinded) 12-week trial of a Mucuna-derived formulation (HP-200) in Parkinson's disease; weaker design than the selected double-blind, controlled trials.
Mucuna pruriens (its irritant spicules) applied topically to the skin to experimentally induce itching, as a model for testing light therapy; not an oral supplement efficacy exposure.

RCT of a multi-herb combination product (Mucuna pruriens, Withania somnifera, Bacopa monnieri, and others) for smoking cessation; effect cannot be attributed to Mucuna alone, and the outcome is unrelated to typical catalog use cases.
